subject: Discovery synthesis & trial commitment — Blueboat
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueboat.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@blueboat.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery synthesis & trial commitment — Blueboat

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick synthesis of what we heard and a proposed trial commitment so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Inference latency spikes on your current hosted stack when session context grows (~300–600ms tail latencies for 1–2 concurrent users).
- Costs for document-processing workloads are unpredictable; you want a predictable per-call price envelope for budgeting.
- Regulatory constraint: a subset of records are PHI and must remain inside a customer-managed VPC, plus KMS-managed keys.

Primary goals for a successful 30-day trial:
1) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 150ms for our baseline prompt set (avg seq length ~220 tokens).
2) Cost: demonstrable unit cost improvement vs current baseline (target: >=25% reduction per 1k tokens for the processed pipeline).
3) Quality: pass prompt-eval suite with no more than 5% regression on intent/slot extraction across the seed dataset.
4) Security: VPC-deployed control-plane with KMS integration for keys; audit log access for the trial.

Pilot scope (proposed):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2 weeks setup + 2 weeks run & eval).
- Model surface: Redwood-hosted model variants we discussed (quantized T-7x and T-13 family for comparison).
- Prompts/evals: we'll run your seed prompt set (we need the 200-record prompt CSV) and our synthetic edge-cases. We will provide a short eval dashboard and regression alerts.
- Owners: Redwood SE (SoojIN) will lead technical onboarding; Priyom will own runtime config & observability; Ben will support cost-modeling and billing conversation. Blueboat owners: Claire (product lead) and Tom (security/infra).

Access / setup checklist we need from Blueboat (to start week 1):
- Short S3 upload with the 200-record prompt set + 2 representative data files (sample names: blueboat_data_sample.csv).
- VPC peering details and a short security profile doc or contact for your infra team.
- Decision on whether you want logging retained in your account or mirrored to Redwood for the trial (we can do either).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (MAPlist + milestone dates) and a sample CSV (blueboat_data_sample.csv).

Proposed next steps / dates:
- Tue Nov 30: Confirm access window & sign MAP.
- Wed Dec 1: Kickoff (30–45m) — environment handoff + role review.
- Dec 1–3: Access provisioning & smoke tests.
- Dec 6–17: Run evaluation & weekly syncs (Tuesdays).
- Week of Dec 20: Final evaluation & quick readout.

If that all looks good I’ll send the MAP link and a calendar invite for Wed Dec 1 10:00–10:30 PST.

Thanks — excited to get moving.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@blueboat.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueboat.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery synthesis & trial commitment — Blueboat

Thanks Soojin — this is a helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Security: we will require KMS-managed keys and prefer that logs are stored in our S3 (retention policy 90 days). Can Redwood support a config where audit logs are delivered to our bucket?
- Data retention: during the trial we need confirmation that no raw PHI leaves our VPC unless encrypted under our KMS.

We are happy with the proposed timeline but two asks: include a short checklist for our infra team (public key, IP ranges for peering, and a simple handshake for KMS access) and can we shift the kickoff to Wed Dec 1 11:00–11:30 PST instead of 10:00? Tom (security) will join and Claire (product) will lead the trial acceptance criteria.

Tom
Tom Alvarez
Head of Infrastructure, Blueboat
tom.alvarez@blueboat.ai | +1 (206) 555-8877

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@blueboat.ai>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@blueboat.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery synthesis & trial commitment — Blueboat

Perfect, thanks Tom — we can support audit-log delivery to your S3 and respect KMS-wrapped PHI boundaries. Quick confirmations and updates below, plus a short infra checklist attached for your team.

Confirmations:
- Logging: Redwood will push structured audit logs to your S3 bucket (we'll need the ARN and a short IAM role we can assume). Logs will be delivered in NDJSON and rotated per your 90-day retention.
- KMS: Onboarding will use customer-managed KMS keys; Redwood will not hold key material. We'll provide the exact KMS policy snippet for your infra to apply.
- Data egress: No unencrypted PHI will leave your VPC; if you choose mirrored logs we will only receive encrypted artifacts under your KMS.

Updated kickoff time: Wed Dec 1, 11:00–11:30 PST — calendar invite to follow.

Infra checklist (high level):
1) S3 bucket name + write permissions for role-redwood-audit (we'll provide role template).
2) KMS key ARN + principal you want Redwood to assume for encryption.
3) IP ranges for the minimal peering (we only need egress to Redwood-managed endpoints for metrics uploads).
4) Contact for your SOC2/security reviewer for the short questionnaire (we can share our SOC2 artifact links).

Next actions (I'll own these with Priyom and Ben):
- Send MAP and DocuSign link by EOD Mon Nov 30.
- Share role template + KMS policy snippet.
- Kickoff invite (Wed Dec 1, 11:00 PST).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’ll attach the infra checklist and MAP in the follow-up mail.

Best,

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
